 Socceroos head coach Tony Popovic has emerged as a potential candidate to take charge of Premier League strugglers Crystal Palace, raising the prospect of a return to his former club.
 According to The Athletic , Popovic is among several names under consideration to replace Pierre Sage, who is reportedly set to become the first Premier League manager sacked this season.

 Sage’s Palace were swept aside 3-1 by Liverpool on Monday (AEDT) – a result that left the 2025-26 Conference League champions bottom of the table through 10 rounds.
 Palace are expected to appoint a successor during the upcoming international break, with former Tottenham boss Thomas Frank, ex-Nottingham Forest pair Sean Dyche and Vitor Pereira, and Coventry City’s Frank Lampard also linked with the job.
 Popovic – who oversaw Australia’s run to the 2026 FIFA World Cup Round of 32 – is reportedly on the list of candidates and it is particularly interesting, given his contract status with the Socceroos after the 2027 AFC Asian Cup was postponed. 
 View this post on Instagram A post shared by Football360.com.au (@football360au) 
 Former Australia international Popovic has strong ties to Selhurst Park, having spent five seasons at Palace between 2001 and 2006, including their successful promotion to the Premier League through the 2004 Championship play-offs.
 He returned in 2011 as assistant coach under Dougie Freedman, helping the club avoid relegation from the EFL Championship.
 The 53-year-old went on to guide Western Sydney Wanderers to the historic 2014 AFC Champions League Elite title, while leading Perth Glory to an A-League Men premiership and Grand Final appearance.
 SOCCEROOS SQUAD: Two sets of brothers, three new faces and eight changes 
 He also coached Turkish club Karabukspor and Greek outfit Xanthi before his most recent club role at Melbourne Victory between 2021 and 2024.
 The reported Palace interest comes amid uncertainty surrounding Popovic’s Socceroos contract following the postponement of the 2027 AFC Asian Cup.
 His agreement was originally set to run until the conclusion of the tournament in Saudi Arabia, scheduled for January-February 2027, raising questions about his future following the change to the international calendar, with the continental competition now slated to start in December next year.
 Popovic remains in charge of Australia and has named a 25-man squad for November’s friendlies against Qatar and Jordan.
